card.name: Words just before a problem to avoid
card.fires_on: Small words and adjectives in administration instructions that come right before a named problem, such as drying, contamination, embolism, pain or interruption. Also "completely" before "dissolved".

modes.label: Purpose phrases
modes.description: Words in "to avoid / to prevent / to minimize" clauses just before the problem is named.
modes.example: To<< prevent>> air embolism, use a non

modes.label: Before a risk noun
modes.description: Linking or modifying word right before a hazard such as contamination or incompatibility.
modes.example: Do not mix with other medications because of the potential<< for>> chemical incompatibility.

modes.label: Completely dissolved
modes.description: The word "completely" before "dissolved" in sublingual dosing directions.
modes.example: Advise patients not to eat or drink anything until the film is<< completely>> dissolved.

card.writes: No clear link between the promoted tokens (mostly "cross" forms) and this pattern, so little clear output effect beyond a weak push toward cross-type words.
card.plain: It lights up on small words in handling instructions just before the text names a problem to avoid.
